Chapter 7: The Role of Values and Meaning in Sustaining Motivation
Once you’ve got the basics of action and focus down, there’s something else that really makes motivation stick—connecting what you do each day to your deeper values, and to things that actually matter to you.
Think about it: procrastination often creeps in when your work feels pointless, or just totally disconnected from your bigger goals. When a task is nothing more than another thing on your to-do list, it’s all too easy to lose steam.
So, how do you get past that? It helps to pause and ask yourself, “Why does this matter to me?” That one question shifts your focus away from the discomfort of the moment, and toward the bigger purpose behind what you’re doing.
Let’s say you’re stuck writing a report. Sure, it might feel tedious right now, but what if you remember that it’s actually tied to helping your team, or maybe moving your career forward? Suddenly, the work has way more meaning.
I like to think of this process as planting a flag on a distant hill. That flag stands for a personal value or a goal that really matters to you. Every small step you take toward it—even the boring or tough ones—starts to feel more significant.
When motivation dips, or you feel the urge to put things off, try taking a moment to reflect on your “why.” It’s a powerful way to reignite your commitment, especially when you’re facing setbacks or running low on energy.
Here are a few simple ways you can connect your daily work to your core values:
Take a minute before you start—think about how this task supports your bigger goals, or the values you care about. Or, jot down a quick note about why the task matters to you, and keep it where you’ll see it. And if doubt creeps in, gently remind yourself of the bigger picture behind what you’re doing.
When you ground your actions in meaning, pushing through discomfort and delays doesn’t feel quite so hard. Suddenly, it’s not just about getting things done—it’s about living in a way that lines up with what truly matters most to you.
